extracted.intended_audience: general readers of mid-20th-century science fiction (Amazing Stories / Project Gutenberg audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A single short science-fiction story ('Step IV' by Rosel George Brown) originally published in Amazing Stories; narrative follows a woman using a multi-step seduction/manual strategy. This is a fiction text rather than an instructional guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step I: A soft answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Step. I. A soft answer turneth away wrath, leaving time for making plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the first step in the protagonist's seduction/manual strategy (printed as a procedural heading in the story). It functions as an admonition to use a gentle response to defuse anger and buy time to act; appears at the start of the narrative section where Juba first meets the man.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule a
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule a--A man pleased with himself is off guard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given immediately after the scene where the man catches a flower and is 'pleased with himself.' In-story guidance: exploiting a man's self-satisfaction provides an opportunity (the narrative shows Juba taking advantage of his complacency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule b
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule b--This is the only time they are tractable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: follows observation of the man's softened face and gentle gaze; the rule indicates that the moment of softness/tractability is rare and should be used strategically. It is part of the protagonist's procedural thinking during seduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule c
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a terse generalization about 'Men' within the manual-like steps Juba recalls/uses; narrative context shows Juba oscillating between seeing this man as different and relying on the general rule that all men share certain traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule d
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule d--A man's ego is his most precious possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used later when Juba observes the man laughing at dawn and considers his display of strength; the rule functions as an instruction to appeal to or manipulate a man's ego as part of the seduction/manual strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: References to Seduction Steps II & III
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of 'Seduction, Step II' and 'Step III' and the caption 'Steps 1, 2 and 3 went according to plan. Then she moved on to....'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story references additional numbered steps (II and III) of a procedural seduction/manual earlier and later in the narrative (e.g., 'She had been prepared for Seduction, Step II...' and later 'instructions for Seduction, Step II' and an enacted Step III moment). These are implied components of a multi-step manual that the protagonist follows, though their full text is not printed on the page; context shows these steps map to conversation (Step II) and the sexual/physical phase (Step III).
